subject: SIG questionnaire: runtime telemetry control ownership & evidence booking
messages:
From: Natalie Chen <natalie@helixsys.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix Systems Security Team <security@helixsys.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: SIG runtime telemetry mapping + evidence timeline

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of Helix Systems' SIG intake we have a focused set of asks around runtime telemetry and control ownership. Specifically we need:

1) Control mapping that ties SIG controls (A1.1, B2.3 style) to Redwood runtime components (serving runtime, batch router, KV cache) and the named owners who can provide evidence.
2) Short samples of telemetry/log output showing token-level latency traces and KV cache hit/miss events (sanitized PII-free).
3) A one-week delivery plan for the artifacts above and a point-of-contact for any follow-ups.

Can you confirm ownership and whether you can provide the evidence by the end of next week? We can accept a combination of XLS mapping + example logs (JSONL). If there are parts that are vendor-controlled (e.g., cloud audit logs) please flag them and we'll accept equivalent attestations.

Thanks,
Natalie
Security Program Manager — Helix Systems

--
This request is scoped to SIG control subset: telemetry, observability, and runtime access.
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie@helixsys.com>
Cc: Helix Systems Security Team <security@helixsys.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG runtime telemetry mapping + evidence timeline

Hi Natalie —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can deliver a control mapping and sanitized telemetry samples. High-level plan:

- Owner mapping: Runtime (Karthik) will cover serving runtime counters and KV cache evidence; Platform Security (Jasmine) will own audit trail and access controls; I will coordinate and assemble the XLS crosswalk.
- Artifacts: an XLS mapping file (control -> component -> owner -> artifact), and a JSONL snippet (redacted) showing token latency traces + cache hit/miss markers.
- Timeline: draft mapping + stub logs by 2028-06-27 close of business; final artifacts by 2028-07-02. If you need an accelerated delivery we can prioritize the most requested controls.

I've looped in Karthik and Jasmine to confirm the artifact formats and any constraints on the logs.

Best,
Sergio
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

---
On 2028-06-25 at 08:14 Natalie Chen wrote:
> Hi Sergio —
> 
> Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of Helix Systems' SIG intake we have a focused set of asks around runtime telemetry and control ownership...
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie@helixsys.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG runtime telemetry mapping + evidence timeline

Thanks — assigning owners here. Quick notes from engineering: 

- We can produce a redacted JSONL showing per-request token latency and a KV cache event field (hit/miss, cache_key_hash). We will strip any user text or prompt content; logs will include only request IDs, timestamps, sequence lengths, per-token latency_ms and cache_event.
- For controls that reference infrastructure audit logs (e.g., host-level syslogs), we will provide vendor references (cloud provider retention screenshot + export) and a compressed CSV export where permitted.
- Attachment plan: I'll upload a draft control crosswalk (redwood_runtime_control_map_v1.xlsx) and a 100-line telemetry sample (telemetry-log-sample.jsonl) to the internal drive and share a link to the Helix team.

Deliverable timeline: draft artifacts for Helix review by EOD 2028-06-27 (as Sergio proposed). If Helix wants evidence in a different schema (SIG standard templates) let us know and we'll map accordingly.

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

--
Forwarded message included below for context.
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie@helixsys.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG runtime telemetry mapping + evidence timeline

Hi Natalie —

Quick security confirmation: the telemetry snippets will be redacted and stored in a locked share with link-only access. We'll apply the standard sanitization runbook (remove prompt/response text, scrub PII fields, aggregate IP addresses to /24). Access will be time-limited and audit-logged; I will be listed as the access approver.

I'll also include a short control narrative for the following SIG questions you often ask:
- How do you correlate telemetry to a specific control owner? (we'll describe the mapping table and owner contact)
- What retention windows apply to raw telemetry vs aggregated traces? (we keep raw ephemeral traces for 30 days, aggregated telemetry metrics for 365 days)

Grace, can you flag any billing/legal holds that might affect generating the CSV exports?

Thanks,
Jasmine
Manager, Platform Security
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie@helixsys.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Draft artifacts uploaded: control map + telemetry sample

Hi all —

I uploaded the draft artifacts to the internal drive: https://redwood-internal.mycompany.com/drive/rt-control-map (link above). Attachments in this thread: redwood_runtime_control_map_v1.xlsx, telemetry-log-sample.jsonl (100 lines).

Notes on the sample logs (first lines shown below):
{"request_id":"r-0001","ts":"2028-06-24T15:02:11.123Z","seq_len":128,"token_latency_ms":[3,2,4,...],"cache_event":"miss"}
{"request_id":"r-0002","ts":"2028-06-24T15:02:12.223Z","seq_len":64,"token_latency_ms":[2,2,1,...],"cache_event":"hit"}

Sanitization: all fields that could contain user text were zeroed; hashes are truncated. If Helix needs a larger sample set or a different anonymization technique (token counts only, no per-token latencies), tell us and we will produce it.

Next step: Sergio — want me to add owner contact emails into the XLS (Karthik/runtime@redwood.com, jasmine.security@redwood.com, sergio@redwood.com) before I share externally?

-Karthik
From: Natalie Chen <natalie@helixsys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft artifacts uploaded: control map + telemetry sample

Thanks Karthik — that looks good. We'll review the drive items and reply with any clarifying asks by Monday 2028-06-30. Two quick asks now:

1) Please add owner contact emails into the XLS (makes our intake reviews faster).
2) For the JSONL sample: can you include a 7-day aggregate summary (median token latency per hour + cache hit rate) as a CSV? That will help our automated tooling ingest the metrics.

If possible include those two items by 2028-06-29; if not, let us know the earliest ETA.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Natalie
Security Program Manager, Helix Systems
